newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end limit down for second day.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end limit down for second day.

text.p: January and March CME lumber futures ended down the $10.00 per thousand board feet daily limit with January down limit for the second day as falling financials added to pressure from weak cash, traders said.

January ended limit down at $389.50 per tbf and March limit down at $377.20. Distant November was also off the limit with other months down $8.40 to $6.60. Trading limits will be expanded to $15.00 Thursday after the two limit losses.
"Mills have overstated their order files -- there is plently of prompt wood showing up," said Curt Cunningham, President of Pacific Futures Trading.
Cunningham also said the break in financials added to the weak undertone in the lumber complex.

"If we are going to have higher interest rates, it's not constructive for home buying and people feel slightly pinched, in terms of net worth. Part of the home buying has been the paper profits on the stock side of the business providing people with a little better net worth," he added.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce unchanged at $407 per tbf, but wholesale trade was cited under $395 per tbf.
In options, January synthetically traded another $6.50 lower and March $2.20 lower.
